To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the attacker's attacking strategy is determined by the extent of applying authentication protocol, which is a function of the system throughput and the security requirement.

(a) The attacker can choose one relay to attack and can make rational decision on the relay selection and the extent of applying authentication protocol to reach the trade-off between the QoS and the security in cooperative communication network; and (b) The attacker's optimal strategy is to select the relay with the highest payoff and to apply the authentication protocol with the lowest cost.
the proposed approach can help the attacker to make rational decision to choose the optimal attacking strategy, which can maximize his payoff, i.e., the extent of system security breach.

how to improve system security in wireless cooperative communication by using the game theoretic approach to analyze attacking strategies of the malicious attacker.
the security provision and QoS in cooperative communication networks.

a game theoretical approach can be applied to quantitatively model and analyze the security provisioning problem in wireless cooperative communication systems.
the attacker's attacking strategies can be determined according to the system's QoS requirement.

a game theoretic framework can be used to quantitatively evaluate the attacking strategies of attacker in cooperative mobile ad hoc networks (MANETs) so as to make a rational decision on applying authentication protocols and relay selection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a relay can be selected to attack in order to maximize the attacker's expected payoff.
a relay can be selected to attack if the relay's attacking cost is less than the cost of applying authentication protocol.
the attacker can make rational decision on the extent of applying authentication protocol to the selected relay so as to make trade-off between security and QoS.
